title: M1 — WHOIS port-43 fallback and full TLD coverage
description:
WHOIS port-43 fallback so any TLD resolves, including ccTLDs with no RDAP service.
Plan: docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 5. Size ~6-9 days, the widest estimate
variance in the plan (see risk register section 12).

Tasks:
- 1.1 internal/whois: port-43 transport (dial, write `domain\r\n`, read to EOF)
  under context deadlines, with a response size cap. Design 8.4
- 1.2 TLD -> WHOIS host discovery via whois.iana.org, cached 24h alongside the
  bootstrap map
- 1.3 Referral chain following, max 2 hops, cycle-detected
- 1.4 Per-TLD quirks table (.de `-T dn,ace`, .jp `/e`) as DATA, not branching
  code -- keeping it a table is what stops it rotting. Design 8.4
- 1.5 Template parsers for the ~40 highest-traffic WHOIS hosts, table-driven
  (label -> field, date layout), in internal/whois/parsers/
- 1.6 Heuristic fallback parser + synonym map, emitting parse_confidence. 8.5
- 1.7 "Not found" signature list per registry -> tri-state `registered`. 8.6
- 1.8 Registry -> registrar RDAP referral following (max 1 hop, degrade to
  registry-only + warning). Design 8.3
- 1.9 domain_availability tool (batch <=50, skips referrals, tighter timeout). 6.1
- 1.10 tld_info tool + whois://bootstrap/tlds resource. Design 6.1-6.2
- 1.11 Fake port-43 listener for tests: slow, truncated, malformed, rate-limited
- 1.12 Golden fixtures per parsed registry incl. "not found" variants,
  testdata/whois/

Exit criteria: the design section 14 TLD matrix (.com .org .uk .de .jp .io .dev
.xn--p1ai, one RDAP-less TLD, one IANA-listed-but-dead TLD) resolves correctly or
degrades to `unknown` with a warning -- never to a wrong yes/no. Suite still
hermetic (no test may reach the network).

Currently stubbed at internal/resolve/resolver.go:88.

Independent of M2 once M0 landed; they share only cmd/whois-mcp wiring and the
Cache interface. Running both in parallel is the one place that removes ~a week.

title: M2 — Authentication: enrollment token to per-session OAuth tokens
description:
Fixed enrollment token entered in a browser yields per-session tokens; /mcp
rejects everything else. Plan: docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 6.
Size ~7-10 days -- the largest bespoke-code milestone and the one where mistakes
are most expensive.

The resource-server half comes from github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/auth
(RequireBearerToken, TokenVerifier, TokenInfo, ProtectedResourceMetadataHandler).
DO NOT reimplement those; verify their signatures against the pinned SDK version
first (current as of v1.7.0). The authorization-server half is ours -- the SDK's
OAuthHandler/AuthorizationCodeHandler are client-side and do not help.

Tasks 2.1-2.15, the load-bearing ones:
- 2.1 Ed25519 keypair load/generate; JWKS at /.well-known/jwks.json with `kid`
  (rotation-ready from the start -- retrofitting kid later invalidates live tokens)
- 2.2 Access token mint/verify: EdDSA JWT, 10 min TTL, verification local with no
  store read (this is what makes replicas stateless)
- 2.3 TokenVerifier: signature, exp, and `aud` equals our canonical URI. The aud
  check is the confused-deputy defence -- one line that must not be skipped
- 2.4 Session store behind an interface; memory impl now, Redis at M3
- 2.5 Refresh tokens: opaque 256-bit, rotating, one-time-use, sliding 30-day
  window; reuse detection revokes the whole family and alerts. Needs its own test
- 2.6 Revocation denylist keyed by sid, TTL = access-token lifetime, hot path
- 2.7 Enrollment secret: Argon2id hash at startup, constant-time compare, per-IP
  rate limit with exponential lockout, audit log that never records the token
- 2.8-2.11 /oauth/authorize (PKCE S256, resource param, code + iss), /oauth/token
  (code exchange + refresh rotation), /oauth/revoke (RFC 7009), /oauth/register
  (DCR back-compat), AS metadata (RFC 8414)
- 2.12 internal/web enrollment UI, go:embed templates, no framework, no build step
- 2.13-2.14 Scopes whois:read / whois:raw / whois:admin, 403 + insufficient_scope
  step-up; rdap_raw + whois_raw behind :raw, session_list/revoke behind :admin
- 2.15 WHOIS_MCP_DEV_STATIC_BEARER, refuses to start unless bound to loopback

Exit criteria: a real MCP client completes 401 -> PRM discovery -> AS metadata ->
browser enrollment -> code + PKCE exchange -> /mcp with a Bearer token. Wrong-aud
tokens rejected; a reused refresh token kills the family; whois:raw with only
whois:read returns 403 with a scope challenge.

Worth a half-day spike first: wire RequireBearerToken with a hardcoded static
token and confirm the 401 challenge and PRM shape against a real MCP client,
before building the bespoke half against it.

Currently stubbed at cmd/whois-mcp/main.go:145 and :152 (loopback-only guard).

title: Security gate — no non-loopback exposure until auth lands
description:
Checkpoint, not a feature: M0 + M1 together are a fully functional COMPLETELY
UNAUTHENTICATED service. Plan: docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 7.

Exposed to a network it is an open proxy querying registries from our egress IP,
and per design section 16 decision 4 we have no registry agreement -- so abuse
through it lands as a block against our own address, presenting as a total outage
for the affected TLD.

Until M2 lands:
- Bind 127.0.0.1 only; the listen address is not configurable to anything else
  while the auth middleware is absent (enforced at cmd/whois-mcp/main.go:145,152)
- No container image built, pushed, or run with a published port
- No kubectl port-forward, no ngrok, no "quick demo" on a shared host

Closing it is the first task of M3 (3.1): the image must fail to start without
WHOIS_MCP_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN, and readyz must fail if auth is disabled while bound
to a non-loopback address.

This bead exists so the constraint is visible in the graph rather than only in
prose, and so nothing downstream of it can be picked up while it is open.

title: M3 — Container and resilience
description:
Hardened image that behaves under load and failure. Plan: section 8. ~4-6 days.

- 3.1 Startup guard: refuse non-loopback bind without an enrollment token
  configured -- this is what closes the section 7 security gate
- 3.2 Multi-stage Dockerfile -> distroless/static:nonroot, CGO_ENABLED=0,
  read-only rootfs. Design 11.2
- 3.3 Redis implementations of Cache and the session store (interfaces already
  exist from P.4 / 2.4)
- 3.4 internal/ratelimit: per-upstream token buckets, exact Retry-After,
  exponential backoff with full jitter. Design 9
- 3.5 Circuit breaker per upstream host, so one dead registry cannot consume the
  concurrency budget
- 3.6 Singleflight collapsing of concurrent identical queries. Design 9
- 3.7 Cache TTL policy table (1h / 5min / 60s / 24h) + max_age_seconds bypass
- 3.8 Prometheus metrics per design 12; OTel tracing with _meta trace-context
- 3.9 compose.yaml with Redis to integration-test the shared-cache path
- 3.10 CI: build image, run compose, end-to-end enrollment + lookup test

Exit criteria: `docker compose up` yields a working enrolled lookup against a
Redis-backed cache; a fake registry returning 429 with Retry-After is honoured
exactly; killing one upstream trips its breaker without affecting other TLDs.

Blocked on decisions: container registry + image naming; Redis managed vs
in-cluster subchart (task 3.3).

title: M4 — Kubernetes: Helm chart and horizontal scaling
description:
`helm install` produces a horizontally scalable deployment. Plan: section 9.
~4-6 days.

- 4.1 Chart scaffold, values.yaml, NOTES.txt documenting the enrollment flow
- 4.2 Deployment >=2 replicas, no PVC; Secret for the enrollment token AND the
  shared Ed25519 signing key -- the signing key MUST be identical across replicas
  or tokens fail on whichever replica did not mint them
- 4.3 Service, Ingress with TLS; HTTP refused outside loopback
- 4.4 NetworkPolicy allowing egress on 443 *and* 43. Design 11.3. Omitting 43
  breaks every ccTLD and reads like a parser bug -- the single highest-value line
  in the chart
- 4.5 HPA on CPU + in-flight requests; PodDisruptionBudget
- 4.6 /healthz liveness; /readyz gated on bootstrap map loaded and cache reachable
- 4.7 JWKS key rotation runbook: publish new kid, wait one access-token TTL,
  retire old
- 4.8 ServiceMonitor when the Prometheus operator is present

Exit criteria: two replicas serve interchangeably with a token minted by either;
a ccTLD lookup succeeds through the ingress, proving port 43 egress; scaling to
zero and back loses no session.

Blocked on decisions: target cluster, namespace, and ingress hostname -- the
hostname is also the OAuth canonical URI and therefore the `aud` value, so settle
it before M2 end-to-end testing rather than during M4. Also: who owns the
enrollment token in production and where it is stored; alerting destination for
refresh-token reuse detection (task 2.5), a credible theft signal that should
page someone rather than only log.

title: M5 — Phase 2 surface: IP/ASN lookups and quirks expansion
description:
ip_lookup / ASN lookups via the RIRs, batch-availability tuning, and per-TLD
quirks expansion driven by whatever the M1 fixture work showed to be missing.
Plan: section 10. ~3-5 days.

Explicitly deferrable: nothing depends on this, and it is the first thing to cut
if the schedule compresses.
